title: A Cipher for the Protocol
premise: Jude Amberdale, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map and in no treaty — is approached by a stranger who claims she once saved his life, a favor she has no memory of performing. The debt he repays is a cipher: an encrypted protocol proving that the Office's director has been selling 'erased' operatives to foreign intelligence services, their memories chemically wiped. As Jude digs into her own missing weeks three years ago, she realizes she may be one of the erased. Hunted by an assassin called Vessel and disavowed by the institution that owns her, Jude smuggles the truth across three capitals, sacrificing allies, her cover, and finally her own carefully constructed identity to broadcast the protocol before the Office can bury it — and everyone who has read it.
about_author: Cyrus Thornbury is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade in cities that appear on no organizational charts. He writes thrillers about institutions that eat their own people, from a farmhouse whose location he declines to confirm.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Jude POV. In Vienna, a soft-spoken stranger named Elias Wren intercepts Jude at a dead drop, thanking her for saving his life in Prague — a city she has no record of visiting. He leaves her a brass key and vanishes. The beat is quiet unease: a crack in the wall of her certainty.

chapters.title: Rules of the Meridian Office
chapters.summary: Jude POV. A day inside the Office shows its machinery: rewritten protocols, redacted rosters, Director Sable Vance's serene control. Jude requests her Prague file and finds it sealed above her clearance — her own clearance. Emotional beat: institutional dread wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Brass and Salt
chapters.summary: Jude POV. The key opens a locker containing a photograph of Jude in Prague, dated during her supposed leave, and a note: 'They took three days from you. I kept the rest.' First flashback fragment surfaces unbidden. Beat: vertigo as memory proves unreliable.

chapters.title: Vessel
chapters.summary: Assassin POV (unnamed). We meet the killer mid-contract in Trieste, methodical and hollow, receiving a new target: the stranger Wren. The assassin's handler speaks only in protocol numbers. Beat: cold competence hiding something almost like grief.

chapters.title: Three Missing Days
chapters.summary: Jude POV. She bribes a retired Office physician who confirms a wipe program codenamed PROTOCOL LANTERN — and that her bloodwork matches its signature. The physician is found dead within hours. Beat: fear turning into resolve; there is no going back to ignorance.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Wren explains himself in a safehouse: he was an erased operative Jude unknowingly extracted in Prague before her own memory was cleaned. His repayment is the cipher — half of it. The other half is inside the Office. Beat: reluctant alliance forged from mutual damage.

chapters.title: Sable's Garden
chapters.summary: Director Vance POV. Vance learns of the breach through channels Jude doesn't know exist. We see her philosophy: erasure is mercy, the Office is order, and order requires pruning. She activates Vessel. Beat: chilling elegance — villainy convinced it is kindness.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Jude POV. Jude and Wren run counter-surveillance through Budapest while decoding the first half of the cipher: names, dates, forty-one erased operatives sold onward. Vessel nearly takes them; Wren is wounded. Beat: the chase becomes real, and so does the trust.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren POV, fevered. While hiding in a river barge, Wren confesses what Jude did for him in Prague — she chose him over orders, then paid for it with three days of herself. Jude overhears. Beat: intimacy born of being seen by someone who knew you before you were edited.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Jude POV. The decoded names implicate liaison officers in three capitals. Jude approaches a British contact, Halloran, who agrees to help — then discovers Halloran is already compromised and must decide whether to burn him or use him. Beat: moral cost of survival arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Pruning
chapters.summary: Vance POV. Vance purges the Office's internal opposition, including Jude's mentor, Marguerite Osei, who dies passing Jude a physical backup of the full cipher. Beat: grief weaponized — the mentor's death converts Jude's mission into a vow.

chapters.title: Half a Truth Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Jude POV. With Osei's backup complete, Jude faces the problem of belief: no government will act on evidence they'll call fabricated. She plans to split the proof across three jurisdictions simultaneously. Vessel closes in. Beat: strategy under pressure, ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Vessel POV. Vessel captures Wren but hesitates when Wren recognizes him — another erased operative, a face from before. The interrogation becomes a conversation between two men missing the same years. Beat: the assassin's mask cracks; he lets Wren escape and reports failure.

chapters.title: Geneva, After Midnight
chapters.summary: Jude POV. First delivery attempt in Geneva fails when the receiving journalist is arrested minutes before contact. Jude realizes Vance has a source inside her plan. Beat: paranoia — every ally now suspect, isolation tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: The Mole in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Wren POV. Evidence points to Jude herself — a conditioned trigger, possibly planted during her erasure, reporting her movements. Rather than confront her, Wren tests it and confirms it. Beat: heartbreak; the person he owes may be the trap.

chapters.title: Lantern
chapters.summary: Jude POV. Jude discovers her own trigger — a phrase Vance uses in routine briefings — and understands she was never just a victim but a designed instrument. She chooses to walk into Vance's office carrying the cipher openly. Beat: agency reclaimed through self-knowledge.

chapters.title: Audience with the Director
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude/Vance POV. A duel of words in Vance's office: mercy versus memory, order versus truth. Vance offers Jude restoration of her missing days in exchange for the cipher. Jude refuses — some prices are paid once, not forever. Beat: climax of ideology before climax of action.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jude, Wren, and a redeemed Vessel POV rotation. The climax: using the Office's own emergency uplink, they transmit the full protocol to press bureaus in all three capitals simultaneously while Vessel holds the door against Vance's security detail. Wren is gravely wounded covering the transmission. Beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Jude POV. The story breaks; governments scramble, denials collapse, Vance resigns rather than face her own tribunal — but not before offering Jude one last erasure, which she declines. Vessel disappears into the world, unburdened. Beat: victory that feels like survival, not triumph.

chapters.title: The Price Itemized
chapters.summary: Jude POV. Funeral for Osei; Wren recovering but changed; Jude formally severed from the Office, stateless by design. She inventories what survival cost — mentor, country, identity — and finds the ledger survivable. Beat: mourning with clear eyes.

chapters.title: A Cipher for the Protocol
chapters.summary: Jude POV. Rebuilding in a small coastal town, Jude receives a package: the last of her Prague memories, recovered from Office archives by an unknown hand. She reads them and finally knows who she was. Beat: memory restored, self chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Jude POV, final chapter. A knock at the door: a frightened stranger holding a brass key, saying someone told them Jude Amberdale settles debts. She looks at the life she built, then packs a bag. Beat: cyclical ending — the price of survival is that you keep paying it forward.
